attack.final_span:
the debut of rookie Filip Zadina, who made the Wings after training camp following what anyone would consider a successful season in Grand Rapids. His 44 goals, 81 points and team MVP award demonstrate that the Wings' 27th overall pick is worth the investment, possibly even earning an additional spot for their young goalie this season; Zadina appears justified in his selection and value.
Here’s what to look for, plus on debut.
News and notes: Remember those busfests when Zadina would travel to and from games in Grand Rapids with defenseman Filip Hronek? That doesn’t happen any longer, with Zadina getting a drive to and from Grand Rapids from Joe Louis Arena. This indicates that vehicle transport is divided into two parts to expedite departures, which could offer some relief to trainer Kevin Neuses. Neuses occasionally accompanied Zadina and Hronek in a car drive, especially when they traveled together.
Which games should I watch for the first appearance of Rasmussen, Zadina, and defenseman Filip Hronek against Dallas, a strong team missing Jamie Benn and its goalie? It’s a high-level snapshot of their situation with the Wings, naturally, as they all face a challenging introduction with Columbus, which plays its first game in two weeks after Sunday’s break.
Filip returns: Zadina joins Tuesday's game in Detroit following his four-goal, four-assist performance last weekend in Grand Rapids, giving him a chance for an NHL roster spot. He had NHL 10 games with Ottawa as a 19-year-old last season and spent 5-6 months in both Grand Rapids and Milwaukee. And had two stints in the NHL last season totaling 25 days. A healthy Zadina would put the Wings in a much better situation with having to choose whether to protect Jakob Trouba or Anthony Mantha.
